arxiv-2107-06671.title: Massive star formation in the Carina nebula complex and Gum 31 – II. a cloud–cloud collision in Gum 31
arxiv-2107-06671.creator: Shinji FUJITA 1∗, Hidetoshi SANO 2, Rei ENOKIYA 3, Katsuhiro HAYASHI 4, Mikito KOHNO 5, Kisetsu TSUGE 6, Kengo TACHIHARA 7, Atsushi Nishimura 8, Akio OHAMA 7, Yumiko YAMANE 7, Takahiro OHNO 7, Rin I. YAMADA 7, Yasuo FUKUI 7
arxiv-2107-06671.description: Abstract We present the results of analyses of the 12 CO ( J J =1–0), 13 CO ( J J =1–0), and 12 CO ( J J =2–1) emission data toward Gum 31. Three molecular clouds separated in velocity were detected at − 25 -25 , − 20 -20 , and − 10 -10 km s -1 .

arxiv-2110-12344.title: A Broader Picture of Random-walk Based Graph Embedding Conference: Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining; August 14–18, 2021; Virtual Event, Singapore Proceedings of the 27th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD ’21), August
arxiv-2110-12344.creator: Zexi Huang, Arlei Silva, Ambuj Singh
arxiv-2110-12344.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zexi Huang, Arlei Silva, Ambuj Singh. Graph embedding based on random-walks supports effective solutions for many graph-related downstream tasks. However, the abundance of embedding literature has made it increasingly difficult to compare existing methods and to identify opportunities to advance the state-of-the-art. Meanwhile, existing work has left several fundamental questions—such as how embeddings capture different structural scales and how they should be applied for effective link prediction—unanswered.

arxiv-2210-13425.title: Molecular-scale substrate anisotropy and crowding drive long-range nematic order of cell monolayers
arxiv-2210-13425.creator: Yimin Luo, Mengyang Gu, Minwook Park, Xinyi Fang, Younghoon Kwon, Juan Manuel Urueña, Javier Read de Alaniz, Matthew E. Helgeson, M. Cristina Marchetti, Megan T. Valentine
arxiv-2210-13425.description: Abstract The ability of cells to reorganize in response to external stimuli is important in areas ranging from morphogenesis to tissue engineering. Elongated cells can co-align due to steric effects, forming states with local order. We show that molecular-scale substrate anisotropy can direct cell organization, resulting in the emergence of nematic order on tissue scales.

arxiv-2211-13244.title: The most massive stars in very young star clusters with a limited mass: Evidence favours significant self-regulation in the star formation processes
arxiv-2211-13244.creator: Zhiqiang Yan ,, Tereza Jerabkova, Pavel Kroupa ,
arxiv-2211-13244.description: Abstract The stellar initial mass function (IMF) is commonly interpreted to be a scale-invariant probability density distribution function (PDF) such that many small clusters yield the same IMF as one massive cluster of the same combined number of stars. Observations of the galaxy-wide IMF challenge this as dwarf galaxies do not form as many massive stars as expected.

arxiv-2405-12291.title: Quantum Lissajous Figures via Projection
arxiv-2405-12291.creator: Errico J. Russo
arxiv-2405-12291.description: Abstract We present and investigate a new category of quantum Lissajous states for a two-dimensional Harmonic Oscillator (2DHO) having commensurate angular frequencies. The states themselves result from the projection of ordinary coherent states (i.e. quasi-classical) onto a degenerate subspace of the 2DHO.

arxiv-2406-12090.title: Data-Aware Hybrid Tableaux
arxiv-2406-12090.creator: Carlos Areces ORCID:0000-0001-7845-8503, Valentin Cassano ORCID:0000-0001-5904-3038, Raul Fervari ORCID:0000-0003-0360-0725
arxiv-2406-12090.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Carlos Areces ORCID:0000-0001-7845-8503, Valentin Cassano ORCID:0000-0001-5904-3038, Raul Fervari ORCID:0000-0003-0360-0725. Labelled tableaux have been a traditional approach to define satisfiability checking procedures for Modal Logics. In many cases, they can also be used to obtain tight complexity bounds and lead to efficient implementations of reasoning tools. More recently, it has been shown that the expressive power provided by the operators characterizing Hybrid Logics (nominals and satisfiability modalities) can be used to internalize labels, leading to well-behaved inference procedures for fairly expressive logics.

arxiv-2407-07624.title: Soft Condensation
arxiv-2407-07624.creator: Ambre Bouillant, Christopher Henkel, Uwe Thiele, Bruno Andreotti, Jacco H. Snoeijer
arxiv-2407-07624.description: Abstract When moist air meets a cold surface, it creates a breath figure characterized by numerous small droplets. The central question is how the vapor flux is distributed between the growth of previously condensed drops and the nucleation of new ones. Here, we investigate the nucleation, growth, and coalescence of droplets on soft crosslinked polymer networks.

arxiv-2408-03700.title: Entanglement Transition due to particle losses in a monitored fermionic chain
arxiv-2408-03700.creator: Rafael D. Soares, Youenn Le Gal, Marco Schirò
arxiv-2408-03700.description: Abstract Recently, there has been interest in the dynamics of monitored quantum systems using linear jump operators related to the creation or annihilation of particles. Here, we study the dynamics of the entanglement entropy under quantum jumps that induce local particle losses in a model of free fermions with hopping and ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} pairing.

arxiv-2409-14055.title: Monitoring Human Dependence On AI Systems With Reliance Drills
arxiv-2409-14055.creator: Rosco Hunter, Richard Moulange, Jamie Bernardi, Merlin Stein
arxiv-2409-14055.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rosco Hunter, Richard Moulange, Jamie Bernardi, Merlin Stein. AI systems are assisting humans with increasingly diverse intellectual tasks but are still prone to mistakes. Humans are over-reliant on this assistance if they trust AI-generated advice, even though they would make a better decision on their own. To identify such instances of over-reliance, this paper proposes the reliance drill : an exercise that tests whether a human can recognise mistakes in AI-generated advice.

arxiv-2503-18485.title: Whispering in Amharic: Fine-tuning Whisper for Low-resource Language
arxiv-2503-18485.creator: Dawit Ketema Gete, Bedru Yimam Ahmed, Tadesse Destaw Belay, Yohannes Ayana Ejigu, Sukairaj Hafiz Imam, Alemu Belay Tessema, Mohammed Oumer Adem, Tadesse Amare Belay, Robert Geislinger, Umma Aliyu Musa, Martin Semmann, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad, Henning Schreiber, Seid Muhie Yimam
arxiv-2503-18485.description: Abstract This work explores fine-tuning OpenAI’s Whisper automatic speech recognition (ASR) model for Amharic, a low-resource language, to improve transcription accuracy. While the foundational Whisper model struggles with Amharic due to limited representation in its training data, we fine-tune it using datasets like Mozilla Common Voice, FLEURS, and the BDU-speech dataset.

arxiv-2509-18106.title: Model-Based Transfer Learning for Real-Time Damage Assessment of Bridge Networks
arxiv-2509-18106.creator: Elisa Tomassini, Enrique García-Macías, Filippo Ubertini
arxiv-2509-18106.description: Abstract The growing use of permanent monitoring systems has increased data availability, offering new opportunities for structural assessment but also posing scalability challenges, especially across large bridge networks. Managing multiple structures requires tracking and comparing long-term behaviour efficiently. To address this, knowledge transfer between similar structures becomes essential.

pmc-10559429.description: BackgroundHere we report the only formally documented case in the United Kingdom, to our knowledge, of a cerebral fat embolism secondary to non-iatrogenic trauma through a Tarlov cyst. This case demonstrates the pathology clearly giving an excellent opportunity to demonstrate a rarely seen pathology as well as illustrating the importance of the patient history to guiding further management.

pmc-11543122.title: Clipping of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm in a toddler: a case report and review of aneurysmal treatment in children
pmc-11543122.creator: George W. Koutsouras, Richmond Mensah, Satish Krishnamurthy
pmc-11543122.description: BackgroundPediatric intracranial aneurysms account for 5% of all aneurysms and less than 10% of all aneurysms cause non-traumatic intracranial hemorrhage in children. They are most commonly secondary to trauma, infection, or genetic etiologies; however, case reports have described iatrogenic intracranial aneurysms.

pmc-11712355.title: Relationships between brain microstructure and Braak Stage progression on the Alzheimer’s disease continuum
pmc-11712355.creator: Lauren A Gitzlaff, Jason F Moody, Yue Ma, Sterling C Johnson, Sanjay Asthana, Tobey J Betthauser, Bradley T Christian, Andrew L Alexander, Barbara B Bendlin
pmc-11712355.description: BackgroundHyperphosphorylation of tau protein underlies the accumulation of neurofibrillary tangles (NFT) in the brain, a neuropathological hallmark of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Braak stages, which reflect the regional spread of NFTs, are defined by NFT presence in the entorhinal cortex (Stages I and II), limbic regions including the hippocampus (III and IV), and neocortex (V and VI).

pmc-12494625.title: The Combination of Chest Wall Perforator Flaps and Surgeon-Performed Breast Ultrasound: An Effective Synergy to Expand the Boundaries of Breast-Conserving Surgery
pmc-12494625.creator: Massimo Ferrucci, Francesco Milardi, Daniele Passeri, Elena Miglioranza, Paola Del Bianco, Giacomo Montagna, Alberto Marchet
pmc-12494625.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIntraoperative ultrasound-guided breast-conserving surgery (IOUS) combined with chest wall perforator flaps (CWPFs) is a promising approach to avoid mastectomy, especially for patients with high anticipated resection-to-breast volume ratios (ARR) who would otherwise be ineligible for breast conservation.MethodsThis study prospectively analyzed surgical, oncologic, and cosmetic outcomes for consecutive patients with stages 0 to III breast cancer who underwent IOUS with CWPF-based partial breast reconstruction at a single institution between 2022 and 2024.ResultsThe study enrolled 73 female patients.

pmc-12643029.creator: Paola Faverio, Lorenzo Del Castello, Maura Spotti, Paola Rebora, Enrico Cesare Maggioni, Raffaele Salerno, Alessandro Perotto, Fabrizio Luppi, Francesco Rocco Bertuccio, Stefania Reale, Valentina Fornari, Filippo Gozzi, Bianca Granozzi, Federico Lorenzo Dente, Francesca Mariotti, Jacopo Simonetti, G
pmc-12643029.description: IntroductionNontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are opportunistic pathogens primarily found in soil and water. Previous studies have linked higher population density and tropical/subtropical climates with increased NTM pulmonary disease (NTM-PD). However, the effects of meteorological parameters and population density on NTM incidence in European countries remain unclear.

pmc-13156236.title: A Large Pedunculated Subserosal Leiomyoma Masquerading as a Pelvic Tumor in Early Pregnancy: A Rare Case Report
pmc-13156236.creator: John Lugata, Felix Luginga, Tecla Lyamuya, Glory Maringo, Eusebious Maro, Alex Mremi, Bariki Mchome
pmc-13156236.description: Uterine leiomyomas, commonly known as fibroids, are the most prevalent pelvic tumors in females, affecting 20%–30% of women of reproductive age. However, large pedunculated subserosal leiomyomas presenting during early pregnancy are uncommon and may mimic adnexal or intra‐abdominal malignancies, posing diagnostic and management challenges.

pmc-13282720.title: Postharvest Quality and Storage Stability of Garlic Cultivars From a Highland Semi‐Arid Region
pmc-13282720.creator: Juliana Araújo da Silva, Maiara Costa Silva, Marília Alves Brito Pinto, Raquel Cardoso Guimarães, Luís Vicente Lima Teixeira, Sabrina Rocha Silva, Quelmo Silva de Novaes, Gisele Brito Rodrigues
pmc-13282720.description: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of storage duration on the physical and chemical properties of garlic bulbs from the Ito and Amarante cultivars, stored in plastic containers under ambient conditions. Temporal analysis was performed using regression models, while differences between cultivars were explored through nonlinear fitting using the LOESS method.

pmc-13379651.title: Deconstructing Pharmaceutical Prices in a Government-Controlled Market: A Hedonic Regression Analysis of B2G Procurement in Thailand
pmc-13379651.creator: Jittakorn Thila, Piriya Pholphirul
pmc-13379651.description: Rising pharmaceutical expenditure poses a persistent governance challenge for public health systems in low- and middle-income countries, yet empirical evidence on pricing in Business-to-Government (B2G) settings remains scarce. This scarcity reflects a fundamental constraint where administrative procurement records are rarely accessible for independent analysis.

pmc-13381685.description: The environmental impact of non-recyclable thermoset waste demands sustainable polymer solutions. Existing dynamic covalent boronic ester chemistries operate at relatively low temperatures (<150 °C), resulting in insufficient stability to meet thermoset performance requirements. Here, we overcome these limitations through a N-iminodiacetic acid (N-IDA) boronate system featuring a strengthened internal B–N coordination bond. This enhanced B–N bond (~1.

pmc-13432439.title: Role of Neuroimaging Before Coronary Angiography in Patients With Out‐of‐Hospital Cardiac Arrest
pmc-13432439.creator: Edmond Wong, Kathryn Yu, Davide Tomassoni, Timothy Scully, Timothy Yeung, Jennifer Cooke, David Tong, Jaya Chandrasekhar, Jason Nogic
pmc-13432439.description: BackgroundPatients presenting following out‐of‐hospital cardiac arrest (OOHCA) often require emergency coronary angiography. Presentations can be associated with syncope or head‐trauma.AimsWe investigated the impact and utility of pre‐coronary angiography CT‐Brain (CT‐B) in patients following OOHCA on clinical outcomes.MethodsRetrospective analysis was undertaken at a large metropolitan hospital to identify patients.

pmc-13536461.title: Comparative Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) Evaluation of Advanced Irrigation Activation Techniques for Bioceramic Sealer Removal in Retreatment: An In Vitro Study
pmc-13536461.creator: Somya Kumari, Rishika Raman, Chi Koy Wang, Binoy K Singh, Abhinav K Singh
pmc-13536461.description: Background: Retreatment cases involving bioceramic (BC) sealers consistently present a major challenge, as residual sealer remnants hinder the efficient cleaning and shaping of the root canals. Removing these sealers is difficult with standard syringe irrigation. To overcome this limitation, irrigant activation techniques have been introduced to help clean otherwise inaccessible areas of the root canal system, particularly the apical third.

pmc-13621396.title: DAMFCMI: capturing cross-view interactions via hybrid attention for circRNA–MiRNA interaction prediction
pmc-13621396.creator: Tao Bai, Xiupan Ma, Lanlan Sun, Zongwen Bai, Wendong Wang, Hang Wei
pmc-13621396.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). MotivationCircular RNAs (circRNAs) and microRNAs (miRNAs) play pivotal roles in gene expression regulation, where understanding their interactions (CMIs) is essential for deciphering the molecular mechanisms behind cellular physiological and pathological states. Most existing approaches to CMI prediction are constrained by their reliance on shallow, single-view representations, while deep models typically align only on final embeddings, thereby neglecting the rich layer-wise interactions that are critical for capturing biological complexity.ResultsTo address these issues, we propose DAMFCMI, a novel method for CMI prediction.
